text: Meanwhile, Magadha kept growing. Its new rulers, the Nanda Kings, were famous for two things,
a gigantic army, and an even bigger treasury. And far to the west, a young king from Macedonia
had just conquered the mightiest empire in the world, Persia. He wanted more. His name
was Alexander. In 326 BCE Alexander crossed into the Punjab. On the banks of
the Jaylam River he fought a king called Porus whose army brought something the
Greeks had rarely faced. War elephants. Alexander won but the Greek writers tell
a famous story about what came next. How do you wish to be treated? Like a king.
Hmm, fair. Keep your kingdom. Then Alexander pushed east to the river Beas, and there his
army simply stopped. They had marched for eight years. They had heard about the Nanda army
waiting beyond, thousands of elephants, hundreds of thousands of soldiers, and the monsoon
rain would not stop. They refused to go any further. Alexander, who had never lost a battle,
had to turn back. Whee! Undefeated. Except by his own tired soldiers. And the weather.
Alexander died in Babylon three years later, at 32. He never saw India again. But a young
One man in India had been watching the Greeks very carefully and he had a teacher with a plan.
